results.text: Comparative efficacy, safety, and kinetics of immediate- and slow-release verapamil in hispanic patients with essential hypertension. We assessed the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of immediate-release (IR) and slow-release (SR) verapamil in Hispanic patients with mild to moderate essential hypertension. Area under the curve and Cmax increased linearly with the dose of IR and SR. Plasma levels showed a more gradual increase and were maintained elevated for longer periods with SR. A double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study of verapamil in exertional muscle pain. Eleven patients, comprising three cases of McArdle's disease and eight with an exertional muscle pain syndrome (EMPS) of unknown cause, entered a double-blind crossover study of verapamil and placebo. None of the patients with McArdle's disease responded to verapamil, but two patients with unclassified EMPS experienced a striking improvement in symptoms and two others showed a partial response.
